questions.q: In the scikit-learn polynomial-fit example, what does the degree-1 (straight line) model demonstrate?
options: Overfitting — it has memorized the noise
A perfect fit to the true curve
Underfitting — it's too simple to capture the curve and has the highest error
Data leakage
questions.explain: A straight line can't capture a curved relationship no matter how it's positioned, so it performs poorly even on the training data — the signature of underfitting.

questions.q: What does the degree-15 model do in that same example?
options: It underfits by ignoring the data entirely
It overfits, bending into a wild shape to chase individual noisy sample points
It produces the most reliable predictions on new data
It behaves identically to the degree-1 model
questions.explain: With enough flexibility, the degree-15 polynomial contorts itself to pass near every noisy sample point, including noise that doesn't reflect the true underlying pattern — classic overfitting.

questions.q: Why can't you diagnose overfitting vs. underfitting by looking at training performance alone?
options: Training performance is always identical regardless of model complexity
Both an overfit and a well-fit model can score well on training data — you need test performance to tell them apart
Training performance is never measurable
Only test performance exists in a real pipeline
questions.explain: An overfit model can score deceptively well on training data by memorizing it. Only comparing against performance on unseen (test) data reveals whether that high score reflects real learning or memorization.

questions.q: A model scores 0.99 on its training set but only 0.61 on its test set. What does this pattern indicate?
options: Underfitting
A well-generalizing model
Overfitting — a large gap between train and test performance
The test set is mislabeled
questions.explain: A large gap between strong training performance and weak test performance is the classic signature of overfitting: the model learned the training set's specifics rather than a generalizable pattern.

questions.q: Which of these is a reasonable fix specifically for an underfitting model?
options: Switch to a more expressive model or add more useful features
Reduce the model to a simpler one
Add regularization to penalize complexity
Train on fewer examples
questions.explain: Underfitting means the model is too simple to capture the real pattern, so the fix is to increase its capacity — a more expressive model or better features — not to simplify it further.
